title: Delegated control plane patterns and operator contracts for regulated private deployments
author: Sana Kapoor
content:
Overview

This document describes a set of pragmatic delegated control-plane reference patterns and associated operator contracts tailored for regulated private deployments (VPC and air-gapped on-prem). It unifies architecture guidance, on-prem packaging constraints, day-2 operational responsibilities, and upgrade/rollback prescriptions into a single operator-facing playbook. The goal is to enable field operators and customer infra teams to run Redwood’s private runtime with minimal custom integration while preserving compliance evidence and predictable SLOs.

Intended audience
- Field operators (Redwood delivery team)
- Customer platform engineers (VPC/on-prem owners)
- SRE/Runbook authors
- Security & compliance reviewers

Key patterns summary
1) Delegated control-plane (lightweight): a small, vendor-managed control plane component runs in the customer VPC but with restricted privileges. Suitable for mid-size regulated customers who accept an audited inbound management channel.
2) Split-control-plane (regional delegation): control functions split across customer-managed and Redwood-managed components; customer retains telemetry aggregation and key management. Best where data residency limits cross-border control traffic.
3) Fully customer-managed control plane: our private package installs a complete control plane in-customer. Redwood provides operator playbooks, CI artifacts, and evidence packages. Required for highly regulated or air-gapped environments.

When to use each pattern
- Delegated: preference for faster onboarding; compliance permits encrypted management signaling to Redwood endpoints; customer accepts KMS-bound provisioning tokens.
- Split: latency-sensitive regions or regulation-driven partial isolation (e.g., EU financial).
- Fully-managed customer control plane: nationalized deployments, air-gapped sites, or customers requiring operator-only access.

Architecture contract (operator responsibilities)
- Ownership boundaries: the document below is an operator contract table describing who owns which component and the required SLAs. Operators must validate each item before commissioning.

Operator contract table (plain text table)
| Component | Owned by | Required SLO / assertions | Evidence artifact |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Control plane API (management) | Redwood (delegated) / Customer (fully-managed) | API availability 99.9% business hours; <250ms median control RPC | k6 probe logs, API traces, uptime report |
| Telemetry aggregator | Customer (split) / Customer (full) | 1-minute ingest latency; sampling config documented | Fluentd/Vector configs, sampling matrix |
| KMS / HSM | Customer | Key rotation <= 90 days; emergency rotation runbook | Rotation logs, key policy doc |
| KV cache persistence | Customer | Snapshot cadence >= 1 per hour; point-in-time restore window 24h | Snapshot index, restore verification report |
| Model artifact store | Customer | Immutable image signing; integrity check on pull | Signed manifest, cosign verification logs |

Network and packaging constraints
- Control plane channel: when delegated, control plane uses an egress-only TLS connection to our management endpoint (mutual TLS). Customers must allow outbound to a small IP range (documented in preflight). No inbound firewall holes required.
- Airgap packaging: operator image bundle (OCI tar + signatures) is produced for customers. Bundle contains: runtime images, cosigned model artifacts, operator CLI tools, validation harness, and a packaged evidence-bundle generator.
- Image signing: cosign v1.6+ recommended. Signatures must be validated during install; verify threshold for operator acceptance is exit code 0 on validation script.

Preflight checklist (customer prerequisites)
1) Confirm KMS/HSM availability and operator permissions.
2) Provide a set of service account principals and RBAC mapping (example in "RBAC snippet" below).
3) Network: outbound egress to management endpoints or physical media transfer process for airgap.
4) Hardware: GPU family compatibility verified (see hardware table).
5) Telemetry: agreement on sampling rate and local retention window (default 7d).

RBAC snippet (YAML example)
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: redwood-operator-binding
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: redwood-operator
    namespace: redwood-system
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: redwood-operator-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io

Minimum hardware and network table (plain text table)
| Category | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU | 1x A10 / A100 equivalent per 2 tenants | 2x A100 per 2 tenants | verify ECC firmware and driver match matrix |
| Disk | 500GB NVMe for model cache | 2TB NVMe for active model pool | throughput 3GB/s recommended |
| Network | 1 Gbps | 10 Gbps for heavy throughput | low jitter network preferred |
| Control plane VM | 2 vCPU, 8GB RAM | 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM | small for delegation mode |

Day-2 operations: operator-runbook (high-level)
1) Normal day checks (daily): verify control plane heartbeat, model cache fullness (<80%), telemetry ingest queue <5000 events.
2) Weekly: run synthetic requests against canary model to validate token-level latency and unit cost regression.
3) Monthly: run signed image refresh and integrity validation; rotate ephemeral certs if configured.
4) After any upgrade: execute smoke verification matrix and preserve evidence bundle.

Incident triage flow (operator decision points)
1) Detect: telemetry alert triggers (latency p95 > 2s or control error rate > 0.5%).
2) Contain: place tenant in safe-mode, activate degraded-model fallback, and throttle noisy tenants.
3) Investigate: collect KV cache snapshot, control-plane traces, and last 50 management RPCs.
4) Remediate: apply rollback or hotpatch per upgrade matrix below.

Upgrade and rollback strategy
- Upgrade types: configuration-only, stateless runtime update, stateful KV/metadata schema migration, model artifact refresh.
- Canary policy: 1% traffic to canary tenant group for 30 minutes with automated rollback if error budget or latency SLO breached.
- Stateful migration safety: maintain dual-read compatibility for 48 hours; snapshot pre-migration and verify checksum post-migration.
- Rollback matrix (plain text)
| Failure class | Immediate action | Rollback safe? | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Control-plane crash | Promote operator safe-mode; fail traffic to local fallback | Yes (stateless) | Verify API probe before reintroduce traffic |
| KV schema corruption | Isolate tenant, restore from snapshot | Yes (requires snapshot) | Preserve corrupted snapshot for forensic review |
| Model quality regression | Route to previous model variant via model aliasing | Yes | Log prompt->response pairs for regression eval |
| Image signature mismatch | Abort deployment, alert security | No (do not rollback unsigned artifacts) | Hold deployment until signed replacement available |

Rollback runbook (step-by-step)
1) Stop rollout: suspend deployment controller.
2) Snapshot runtime state (if possible): export KV, active model list, and sockets.
3) Switch traffic: update routing config to previous model/service tag.
4) Validate: run smoke tests (generation, embeddings, latency) for 15 minutes.
5) If OK: mark release as reverted and file_issue with failure artifacts. If not OK: escalate to Engineering (oncall) and open incident.

Telemetry and evidence collection
- Required telemetry streams: control-plane traces, model invocation traces (sampling 1:100 by default), node-level metrics at 10s granularity, operator audit logs.
- Evidence bundle: after any major upgrade or incident, generate a signed bundle containing: snapshot metadata, cosign verification logs, canary probe results, and a short runbook note. Bundle filename pattern: evidence-<tenant>-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz.sig

Operator CLI common commands
- preflight check: ./redwood-operatorctl preflight --config site-config.yaml
- install (delegated): ./redwood-operatorctl install --mode delegated --accept-evidence --kubeconfig /path/to/kubeconfig
- bundle verify (airgap): ./redwood-operatorctl verify-bundle /tmp/redwood-bundle.tar.gz
- generate evidence: ./redwood-operatorctl evidence --dir ./evidence --since 2026-03-01

Testing and validation suite (recommended)
- Synthetic traffic harness: 10k short prompt generative workload, 1k embeddings workload, 100 long-context (8k tokens) samples. Collect latency P50/P95, token cost, and quality metrics (perplexity, top-k stability).
- KV consistency checker: ensure no drift between primary and restored snapshot; script exit 0 required.

Template handoff artifacts (what engineers should supply)
- site-config.yaml (templated): contains role bindings, endpoints, and telemetry targets.
- operator-perm-assertion.txt: list of required RBAC checks.
- canary-test-suite.yml: canary validation jobs.
- cosign-public-keys.pem: keyset for signature verification.

Related pages and references
- See also: private-deploy-commissioning-and-safety-gate-playbook (customer onboarding), runtime-artifact-provenance (signing). These internal references should be used during customer engagements.

FAQ (short)
Q: Can customers opt out of outbound management channel?
A: Yes — choose the fully-managed customer control plane pattern; airgap bundles and operator-only workflows are supported.

Q: What is the expected time to revert a bad stateless rollout?
A: Typical revert window for stateless runtime is <10 minutes (control plane reaction + routing update). Stateful rollbacks depend on snapshot size and verification and typically take 30–120 minutes.

Ownership and next steps
- Owner: eng-private-deployments (operator enablement)
- Action items before publication: fill the IP egress allowlist for delegated control endpoints, publish signed airgap bundles for the next release, and run operator game-day against the canary policy.

Appendix A: example smoke test checklist
1) Generate 100 prompts against the canary model; verify median latency < 350ms and no errors.
2) Run embeddings job: 50 vectors; verify similarity index within expected range.
3) Validate cosign signatures on images used in rollout.
4) Confirm evidence bundle creation and signature.
